purpose: Curated, web-verified catalog of GOVERNED data-acquisition tools for WALTEUR DISCOVER/RESEARCH (and VERIFY) phases. A build that pulls external web/file data must route through one of these vetted tools (enforced by data-acquisition-gate.sh). KEY PRINCIPLE: the license is usually clean, but the USAGE (robots.txt / ToS / anti-bot circumvention / PII) is the real legal exposure for a $50-100M product — hence the per-tool risk + governance fields and the stealth-requires-signoff policy.

policy.default_posture: respect robots.txt; per-domain allowlist; rate-limit; PII scan on captured content; audit every fetched URL via a source receipt
policy.high_risk_definition: any tool whose core/optional capability defeats a site's bot defenses (TLS/JA3 impersonation, fingerprint spoofing, auth/login bypass, CAPTCHA solving) — using it can breach ToS and implicate anti-circumvention/CFAA-style claims
policy.prefer: compliant first-party APIs and robots-respecting fetchers over maximal evasion; reserve high-risk tools for owned/authorized/explicitly-signed-off sources only

tools.name: Firecrawl
tools.license: AGPL-3.0 (core engine) / MIT (SDKs + official MCP server)
tools.mcp: firecrawl-mcp (npm, MIT) — scrape/map/search/crawl/extract/agent; native Claude Code plugin + Docker image mcp/firecrawl
tools.anti_blocking: stealth (hosted tier) — but respects robots.txt by default
tools.when_to_use: PRIMARY governed web->markdown/JSON acquisition during DISCOVER/RESEARCH: competitor docs, API specs, market data; schema-driven structured extraction; whole-site map.
tools.governance: Prefer the hosted API or the MIT MCP client to avoid AGPL copyleft attaching to WALTEUR's self-hosted code. Respects robots by default; ToS/copyright/PII remain the operator's responsibility. Hosted API sends target URLs+content to a third party (PII/DPA consideration for regulated data).

tools.name: Crawl4AI
tools.mcp: first-party MCP server in the Docker image (SSE http://localhost:11235/mcp/sse; tools: md/html/screenshot/pdf/execute_js/crawl/ask)
tools.anti_blocking: stealth optional (undetected-Chrome, proxy escalation) — OFF by default per policy
tools.when_to_use: PRIMARY self-hosted, key-free page->markdown engine when data must stay inside the perimeter; high-throughput batch crawls (arun_many) of public docs.
tools.governance: Apache-2.0 is commercial-safe. Does NOT enforce robots.txt by default — WALTEUR must run it in robots-respecting mode, stealth OFF, per-domain allowlist + rate-limit, PII scrub downstream. Stealth/undetected-Chrome is high-risk if enabled — treat as signoff-gated.

tools.name: MarkItDown
tools.when_to_use: NORMALIZATION stage after a fetcher pulls raw bytes: convert spec PDFs, Office docs, slide decks, fetched HTML into token-efficient markdown for agent context.
tools.governance: MIT, commercial-safe. No crawling => robots/ToS risk is on the supplied URL, not here. PII risk is content-side (OCR/transcription can surface PII) => apply output redaction. Optional Azure backend (OFF by default) transmits content to Azure (DPA/residency review).

tools.name: Scrapy
tools.category: industrial bulk crawler (static/semi-static HTML at scale)
tools.anti_blocking: polite only (AutoThrottle, DOWNLOAD_DELAY, rotating UA/proxy via middleware) — no native evasion
tools.when_to_use: Heavy-duty bulk acquisition of many static pages once a target set is known; scheduled/recurring scrape pipelines with retries/throttle/dedup.
tools.governance: BSD, commercial-safe. FORCE ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True (library default is False), set an identifying User-Agent, keep AutoThrottle/DOWNLOAD_DELAY on. Wrap in a domain allowlist + PII filter; framework adds no legal protection.

tools.name: browser-use
tools.anti_blocking: real-browser inherently defeats JS/basic bot checks; hosted adds stealth/proxy/CAPTCHA (HIGH-RISK — keep OFF)
tools.when_to_use: FALLBACK for data behind login or heavy JS that HTTP fetchers can't reach — ONLY on sites the customer owns or is explicitly authorized for. Not the default crawler.
tools.governance: HIGH-RISK: impersonates a human, can bypass login walls, robots NOT honored by default. Run only against owned/authorized targets; stealth/proxy/CAPTCHA OFF without legal sign-off; PII filter on captured content. License MIT (clean); the USAGE is the exposure.

tools.name: Crawlee
tools.mcp: none first-party (Apify platform MCP exposes Crawlee-based Actors separately)
tools.anti_blocking: strong: proxy rotation, session pools, zero-config human-like fingerprint generation (HIGH-RISK)
tools.when_to_use: In-process resilient large-scale crawling needing proxy rotation/retries/queue management, beyond single-URL fetch.
tools.governance: HIGH-RISK: fingerprint spoofing + residential-proxy rotation are designed to defeat bot defenses (ToS/CFAA/anti-circumvention exposure). Apache-2.0 license is clean. DISABLE fingerprint spoofing by policy; enforce robots/allowlist/rate-limit; Apify proxy adds a third-party data-processor (DPA/GDPR review).

tools.name: curl_cffi
tools.anti_blocking: core purpose: impersonates Chrome/Firefox/Safari TLS+JA3/JA4 + HTTP/2/3 to defeat Cloudflare/Akamai/DataDome (HIGH-RISK)
tools.when_to_use: Low-overhead governed fetch transport for sites that block plain requests, WITHOUT a full browser — only for explicitly-approved sources. Pairs with autoscraper for selector-free pattern extraction.
tools.governance: DUAL-USE / HIGH-CAUTION: the entire value is misrepresenting client identity to defeat bot detection — frequently violates ToS and may implicate anti-circumvention/CFAA. MIT license clean; USE is the exposure. Mandatory: domain allowlist + robots/ToS pre-check + rate-limit + PII redaction + per-source legal sign-off.

tools.name: AutoScraper
tools.when_to_use: Learn extraction rules from a few example values, then extract the rest of a page/site without hand-written selectors. Pair with a governed fetcher (curl_cffi/Firecrawl) as the transport.
tools.governance: MIT, commercial-safe. Parser only — robots/ToS risk is on the paired fetcher, not here. PII risk is content-side.

not_data_tools.name: The Agency (agency-agents)
not_data_tools.note: 232 markdown agent-persona templates across 16 divisions — NOT a data-acquisition tool (no web/file access). Relevant only as idea-mining for WALTEUR's persona layer, which is already mature + gate-driven. Lifted into personas.json only if a specific role is missing.
